purpose: Canonical operating system for Applied Practical Thinking doctrine, standards, reusable agent capabilities, platform adapters, and standards distribution tooling.
description: This repository is a documentation and asset toolkit with dependency-free Node.js validation and lifecycle commands. It is not a long-running application: maintainers run validators, generators, audits, installers, and synchronization commands against this repository or downstream project repositories.

architecture.summary: Human-authored canonical doctrine and reusable assets feed manifests, validators, installers, and tool-specific adapter surfaces; generated catalogs and archives remain non-authoritative projections or historical evidence.
components: Principles and standards define canonical judgment and required practice.
Structured taxonomy and publication contracts define how canonical guidance is classified and which reviewed artifacts may appear on public surfaces.
Skills, agents, prompts, templates, examples, checklists, context, and routing provide reusable operational capabilities.
Manifests select installable bundles while installers and scripts validate, distribute, scan, synchronize, and repair managed assets.
Platform directories adapt canonical assets for Codex, Claude, Gemini, GitHub Copilot, VS Code, and local-model consumers.
Documentation, references, product hubs, and knowledge assets support adoption, contracts, and retrieval without replacing canonical sources.
architecture.runtime_model: On-demand Node.js command-line scripts and PowerShell/Bash wrappers; no resident process, API server, database, or local web server.
architecture.deployment_model: Assets are installed or synchronized into independent target repositories through manifests and lifecycle commands. The repository itself has no production deployment target.

runtime.summary: Run means invoking repository checks, catalog and inventory generators, workspace audits, or downstream asset lifecycle commands. There is no application build or server startup path.

requirements.name: Node.js
requirements.recommended: Node 20 or newer in operator documentation; CI verifies Node 22

requirements.name: PowerShell or Bash
requirements.declared: Required only for the matching lifecycle wrapper
requirements.recommended: Use the native shell for the current platform

runtime.package_manager: npm scripts orchestrate dependency-free Node.js tooling; no application dependency installation is required by the documented checks.
runtime.local_server: Not applicable; this repository does not expose a local application server.
runtime.build: Not applicable as an application build. Catalog and inventory generation produce documentation projections.
runtime.deployment: Not applicable for the repository. Distribution targets are independent downstream repositories.

commands.name: Repository completion gate
commands.purpose: Run repository validation, metadata validation, manifest parity, content-specialization checks, project inventory checks, and lifecycle tests.

commands.name: Repository structure validation
commands.purpose: Validate metadata, required directories, asset contracts, links, catalogs, migration provenance, and retired interfaces.

commands.name: Project profile validation
commands.purpose: Validate the repository's canonical structured project profile.

commands.name: Content specialization validation
commands.purpose: Prevent unreviewed growth or substitution in thin shared-core skills, agents, principles, and prompts while preserving independently consumable contracts.

commands.name: Installer and inventory tests
commands.purpose: Exercise asset lifecycle behavior and project inventory validation, rendering, discovery, and stale-output checks.

commands.name: Generate repository context
commands.purpose: Render docs/project-context.md from the canonical version-2 JSON profile.

commands.name: Check repository context
commands.purpose: Fail when the generated repository context differs from its canonical JSON profile.

commands.name: Generate workspace inventory
commands.purpose: Discover sibling projects and render the workspace inventory using verified, legacy, and pending status labels.

commands.name: Workspace standards audit
commands.purpose: Assess sibling repositories for APT installation and readiness signals.

commands.name: Detect target needs
commands.purpose: Recommend relevant manifests from target repository evidence.

commands.name: Install assets preview
commands.purpose: Preview a first-time manifest installation without changing the target.

commands.name: Install assets
commands.purpose: Install selected managed assets and create the target-owned installation record.

commands.name: Scan managed assets
commands.purpose: Report missing, changed, and current managed artifacts.

commands.name: Synchronize managed assets
commands.purpose: Update managed assets while preserving locally changed files.

commands.name: Repair managed assets
commands.purpose: Force reviewed repairs with backups after drift has been assessed.

commands.name: Application build
commands.purpose: Not applicable; this repository is not an application artifact.

commands.name: Application server
commands.purpose: Not applicable; repository operations are on-demand commands.

commands.name: Production deployment
commands.purpose: Not applicable; managed assets are distributed to independently owned target repositories.

structure.purpose: Durable canonical APT doctrine organized by the four pillars and supported domains.
Required practice plus compact installable summaries.
Canonical accountable roles and review perspectives.
Reusable model instructions, starter artifacts, demonstrations, and verification gates.
Selective context, model and task routing, and portable knowledge projections.
Tool-native adapters and distribution surfaces for supported AI platforms.
Bundle selection, compatibility wrappers, validation, generation, audit, and asset lifecycle tooling.
Machine-readable contracts, schemas, vocabularies, design tokens, canonical taxonomy, and public publication selection.
Repository operations, adoption guidance, architecture diagrams, migration records, and generated distribution catalogs.
Audience-layered product documentation patterns and repository governance artifacts.
Historical provenance, retired tooling, and preserved consolidation evidence.

integrations: GitHub Actions validates Linux and Windows behavior with Node.js 22.
Target repositories consume selected manifests through Node.js commands or PowerShell/Bash wrappers.
Codex, Claude, Gemini, GitHub Copilot, VS Code, and local-model adapters consume tool-specific platform surfaces.
The sibling applied-practical-thinking site reads references/publication-manifest.json and references/apt-taxonomy.json to generate a curated public reference library.

canonical: principles/ owns doctrine and judgment guidance.
skills/ and agents/ own provider-neutral operational capabilities and accountable roles.
Target repositories own their local product context, architecture decisions, commands, integrations, and exceptions.
generated: docs/distribution/*-CATALOG.md files are generated projections and must be regenerated from authored assets.
Workspace inventory Markdown is generated from child-repository profiles.
Public APT Markdown, manifest, and taxonomy projections in applied-practical-thinking are generated from explicit canonical contracts.
graphify-out/ and other analysis outputs are discovery artifacts, not canonical sources.
archived: docs/archive/ preserves historical provenance and retired interfaces and must not be treated as active guidance.

constraints: Do not edit generated catalogs, copied publication assets, build outputs, or graph outputs as source.
Keep canonical principles separate from procedures, examples, prompts, adapters, and archived history.
Preview target-repository lifecycle changes before applying them; forced repair requires reviewed drift and backups.
Do not infer target product behavior or exceptions from this reusable standards repository.
Public publication defaults to internal and requires affirmative selection through references/publication-manifest.json.
Run npm run check before claiming repository changes are complete.

architecture_pattern: Canonical documentation and reusable agent assets with manifest-driven distribution and dependency-free Node.js governance tooling
command_matrix: See commands[] in this version-2 profile.
validation_evidence: npm run check and cross-platform GitHub Actions
release_model: Repository revisions plus downstream manifest installation or synchronization
operations_model: Detect, preview, apply, verify with drift preservation and forced-repair backups
ai_agent_usage: Provider-neutral skills, accountable agent roles, routing guidance, context packs, prompts, and tool-specific adapters
security_model: No application runtime or stored customer data; security depends on source review, manifest boundaries, target-owned secrets, and high-accuracy escalation rules
learning_value: Demonstrates separation of doctrine, operational capabilities, adapters, generated projections, provenance, and downstream adoption records

showcase.summary: Canonical APT doctrine and reusable agent operating system with governed, manifest-driven distribution.
